creator: Dan McCreary
subject: TM1637

description: Connect the four pins of a TM1637 display module to the correct Raspberry Pi Pico pins; correct wires lock in and the display lights up 12:34.

educational.topic: Wiring a TM1637 display to the Pico
learningObjectives: Apply a wiring table by connecting each module pin to the correct Pico pin
Distinguish power, ground and GPIO pins on the Pico pinout
Explain why the module is powered from 3V3(OUT) instead of VBUS
prerequisites: Pico pin names and physical pin numbers (Chapter 2)

keyQuestions: Why is any GND pin acceptable but only one power pin?
What would change in the code if CLK used GP6 instead of GP2?
Why is 3.3 V safer than 5 V for the Pico's signal pins?
commonMisconceptions: Pin 4 means GP4 (physical pin 4 is GP2)
VBUS and 3V3(OUT) are interchangeable power pins
assessmentOpportunities: The student wires all four pins correctly without Show answer.
The student explains why a signal pin must never go to power or ground.
The student explains that any GND pin works but VCC must use 3V3(OUT).
